THIS APPEAL HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT AND COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT THIS DAY THROUGH VIDEO CONFERENING AT KALABURGI, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 10.03.2017 passed in MVC No.1622/2013 by the learned Principal District and Sessions Judge and MACT-I, Hassan, dismissing the claim petition for compensation on account NC: 2023:KHC:40572 of the death of 1st petitioner's wife Rajamma in road traffic accident, the petitioners have approached this Court in appeal.
2.

It is the case of the petitioners who are the husband and children of one Rajamma that, on 21.04.2013 at 7.30 p.m., after attending a marriage reception program at Arasikere, Rajamma along with her son-in-law Papaiah and 3rd petitioner, returned to Hassan in train and her son- in-law dropped his wife- 3rd petitioner, to their home on his motorcycle.

While returning back to Railway Station to take Rajamma to his home, he saw that Smt. Rajamma, was walking from Railway Station on B.M.Road and infront of Mithra Granite, towards Dairy circle, the rider of motorcycle bearing No. KA-19-L-2912, came in rash and negligent manner and dashed to her resulting in severe head injury.

Immediately, she was taken to Government Hospital, Hassan and as advised by the doctors,

2 was taken to NIMHANS, Bangalore; she was treated in the said Hospital, discharged and again admitted to Government Hospital NC: 2023:KHC:40572 Hassan.
However, on 10.05.2013, she succumbed to injuries sustained in the accident.
The petitioners contended that they incurred Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, Rs.50,000/- towards obsequies, the deceased was aged 45 years, earning Rs.10,000/- per month.

The said motorbike belonging to respondent was insured with 2nd respondent and therefore, they are entitled for compensation from respondents 1 and 2.
3.
On issuance of notice by the Tribunal, respondent No.1, though appeared through his counsel, has not filed objections.
Respondent No.2 denied that deceased Rajamma was pedestrian, hit by vehicle bearing KA-19-L- 2912, ridden by 1st respondent but admitted it was insured with it.

It was contended that the petitioners and respondent No.1 colluded with each other to fix vehicle in the alleged accident and they have lodged a false complaint 4 days after the accident to make unlawful gain.

Subsequently, respondent No.2 by amending the statement of objections has taken up specific defence that, Rajamma NC: 2023:KHC:40572 was not a pedestrian, but she was a pillion rider of the two- wheeler belonging to her son-in-law and the alleged accident was due to rash and negligent riding of the bike by Papaiah.

It was also contended that the compensation claimed is excessive,
exorbitant, and prayed to dismiss the petition.
4. On the basis of the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the appropriate issues and petitioner No.1 was examined as PW1 and one witness was examined as PW2 and Exs.P1 to P23 were marked.

Respondent No.2 has examined its official as RW1 and got marked Exs.R1 to R6.
5.
The Tribunal after hearing both sides, dismissed the petition on the ground that the accident involving the vehicle of the respondent No. 1, insured by respondent No. 2 is doubtful.
6. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the petitioners have approached this court in appeal.
On issuance of notice, respondent No.1 - Insurance Company appeared through its counsel and respondent No.2 despite service, remained unrepresented.
On admitting the appeal, the Tribunal records have been secured.

8. Heard the arguments by learned counsel for both sides and perused the Tribunal records.
9.

The learned counsel appearing for the appellants/petitioners submitted that the emergency case record of NIMHANS Hospital, clearly depict that the accident occurred while the deceased Rajamma was crossing a road as a pedestrian.
However, the subsequent case sheet of the NIMHANS show that the deceased was a pillion rider and the motorcycle hit to another two wheeler.
It is submitted that this by itself cannot be a ground to reject the petition.

It is submitted that the history stated before the official of the NIMHANS at the time of the admission is borne out of the emergency case record which was handwritten document, which was part of the case sheet NC:
2023:KHC:40572 and it clearly mentioned all the particulars of the accident.

The said record was Rajaiah vs The Manager on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191853068/
3 prior to the deceased was taken to ward, before she was subjected to the surgery at NIMHANS.

sentences.text: Therefore, he submits that the two records of the NIMHANS hospital produced by the respondent-insurance company itself goes to show that the first information which was given at the time of admission to the hospital is on 21.04.2013 at 11.49 hours, which was Sunday.
Thereafter, the deceased Rajamma was taken to neuro surgery and the Ex.R2 show that she underwent Craniotomy for evacuation of SDH and the entry was on 22.04.2013 at 1.32 a.m.
Thereafter the Ex.R4 obviously at the ward, stated that the deceased Rajamma was pillion rider and it hit to another two wheeler.
Therefore, the mention of the word pillion rider can only be found in the subsequent records of the NIMHANS but not the record which was written at the time of admission to the hospital.
In that view of the matter, he submits that the information which was given at the time of the admission is relevant and that should have been considered by the Tribunal.
Secondly he contends that the delay of 4 days in filing the FIR could have been inferred to be for the purpose of implicating the respondent No.1 and 2.

He submits that the deceased Rajamma suffered the accident at about 7.00 p.m. and on the same day, she was taken to Government Hospital, Hassan and thereafter, she was shifted to NIMHANS on the same night.

Therefore the Trauma on the family of the deceased should have been borne in mind by the Tribunal and he submits that the family members were engaged in the treatment of the deceased Rajamma and therefore the delay of 4 days in filing the complaint could not have been considered to be the ground for dismissal of the petition.
He further submits that the complainant Papaiah, who was none else than the son-in-law of the deceased was engaged in the treatment and he was first person who had seen the accident.
Therefore, he went with the deceased Rajamma to NIMHANS hospital and he could not have lodged the complaint to the concerned police.

Thirdly he contended that the trial Court, has accepted the version of the respondent No.2-insurance company that the NC:
2023:KHC:40572 deceased Rajamma, the wife of Papaiah were pillion riders on the motorcycle driven by Papaiah and the accident occurred due to the negligence of the said Papaiah.
There is no material on record to show that the wife of Papaiah as well as deceased Rajamma were the pillion riders of the motorcycle ridden by Papaiah.

11. Under these circumstances, the conclusions reached by the Tribunal are nothing but product of fertile imagination and there being absolutely no evidence on the part of the respondents to show that Rajamma was also the pillion rider of the motorcycle driven by Papaiah, it was not proper for the Tribunal to reject the petition.

Further, he contends that the deceased was aged about 58 years as per the PM report and therefore the notional income should have been considered and adding conventional heads, the adequate compensation should have been granted by the Tribunal.

Secondly,
he contends that the registration number of the motorcycle of the complainant Papaiah is not at all mentioned in the complaint.
Thirdly, he points out that the motorcycle of respondent No.1 was examined after 30 days and it is surprising that the damages to the said vehicle were still available.

He submits that the medical records of the NIMHANS Hospital show that Rajamma was a pillion rider and therefore it can safely be concluded that Papaiah rode the motorcycle with two pillion riders from Railway Station to his house, on the way of Rajamma fell down and sustained injuries.
Therefore he supports the view taken by the Tribunal.
13. The first aspect to be considered by this Court is regarding the accident.
The petitioner No.1 was examined as PW1 and an eye witness to the accident as PW2.
The PW1 was not an eye witness to the accident and therefore - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:40572 his evidence is not of much relevance.
However in the cross-examination, it was elicited that his son-in-law i.e. Papaiah was bringing his wife on his bike.
This cannot be construed to be an admission by PW1 that Rajamma was the pillion rider of motorcycle of Papaiah.
He was not an eye witness to the accident.

It has come in the evidence as well as in the FIR that the said Papaiah had taken his wife to his house and had dropped her and thereafter he was returning to the Railway Station in order to take the deceased Rajamma to his house.
Obviously the say of PW1 that his son-in-law Papaiah was bringing his wife to his house was without seeing the spot and Rajamma being the pillion rider of the motorcycle of the said Papaiah.
14. The evidence of PW2-Venkatesh shows that he is not related to the petitioners in any way and he was an eye witness to the accident and he has not lodged any complaint to the police.
It is not necessary that a bystander who had seen the accident should have lodged the complaint to the police.
In the cross examination of the - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:40572 PW2, it appears that there was nothing to show that he was in any way related to or acquainted with the petitioners.

15. The FIR produced at Ex.P1 and complaint at Ex.P2 show that the complaint was lodged on 25.04.2013 and it was stated that he, his wife Rajamma had gone to the marriage of their relative at Arasikere and returned and alighted at Hassan Railway Station and the complainant had parked his bike at the Railway Station and he had taken his wife on the motorcycle and dropped her at his house and then he was returning to Railway Station to take the deceased Rajamma.
While returning to Railway Station he found that Rajamma was walking in front of Mithra Granites and a motorcycle came from Railway Station side and dashed against Rajamma causing the accident.
It was at about 7.30 p.m. and immediately the deceased Rajamma was taken to Govt. Hospital Hassan and for further treatment she was taken to NIMHANS on the same night.

However, he mentioned the Rajaiah vs The Manager on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191853068/
5 number of motorcycle which caused the accident as KA-19-L-2912.

It is also stated that Rajamma was unconscious.
16. The other police papers which are produced at Ex.P3 and the charge sheet at Ex.P6 also show that investigation was conducted by the police.
The mahazar of seizure of motorcycle show that the motorcycle had damages on the front.
The charge sheet produced at Ex.P6 show that the deceased Rajamma succumbed to the injuries on 10.05.2013 at Govt. Hospital, Hassan.
17. The respondent No.2-insurance company has produced the entire case sheet of NIMHANS which show that she was taken to the hospital on 21.04.2013 at 11.49.25 seconds on Sunday.
In this 'EMERGENCY TRAUMA CARE RECORD', (which is in the yellow sheet of paper) show that the time of the injury was stated to be 21.04.2013 at about 7.00 p.m.
It was mentioned that it was a road traffic accident and the pedestrian when - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:40572 crossing the road was hit by two wheeler near Hassan Dairy Circle.
It was noted that there were injuries on the tempero parietal area and it was sutured and there was history of vomitting.
It is to be noted that based on this emergency trauma record, the other records of the hospital were prepared.
Obviously Ex.R2 admission record was prepared on 22.04.2013 at 1.32 a.m.
Thereafter, she was taken to neuro surgery and after the surgery she was taken to the ward.
The next sheet of the Emergency Trauma record prepared at Head and Spine Trauma Centre show that the 'history the road traffic accident with two wheeler pillion rider; hit to another two wheeler'.
It is to be noted that except this, there is nothing on record in the entire case sheet to show that the deceased Rajamma was pillion rider of a motorcycle.
It is not known how divergent facts are mentioned in the admission record of the hospital.
Any how the first information which was collected by NIMHANS as per the Emergency Trauma Care record has to be accepted.
The MLC record of the Chamarajendra Hospital / Government Hospital, Hassan had been summoned by the Tribunal.
The said record shows that the history was stated to be RTA near Dairy circle hit by a bike at 7.30 p.m.
This document no where mentioned that Rajamma was a pillion rider and the injury was due to fall.

19. The evidence of RW1, who is an official of the respondent No.2-insurance company shows that deceased Rajamma was the pillion rider of the motorcycle of her son- in-law Papaiah and it met with an accident and therefore she was taken to the Govt. Hospital, Hassan and thereafter to NIMHANS Rajaiah vs The Manager on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191853068/
6 Bangalore.
She was in patient from 22.04.2013 to 08.05.2013 at NIMHANS and thereafter she was shifted to Govt. Hospital, Hassan where she succumbed to the injuries.
Therefore, RW1 contends that the vehicle belonging to the respondent No.1 was not involved in the accident.
It is pertinent to note that Ex.R1 is the medical records of deceased Rajamma which was summoned by the insurance company.
The source of the information that - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:40572 deceased Rajamma was the pillion rider of the motorcycle ridden by Papaiah is not disclosed by the RW1 in his evidence.
20. The learned counsel appearing for the appellants has placed reliance on the decision in a case Ravi vs. Badrinarayan and Others1.
In the said decision, the claim petition was rejected by the Tribunal as well as the first appellate Court.
When the matter was considered by the Apex Court, it was noticed that the delay in filing the FIR alone cannot be a ground to doubt the accident itself.

In para 21, it was stated as below:
"The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same (2011) 4 SCC 693 - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC:40572 should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquility of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if, there is delay, the same deserves to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons."

21. From the above evidence on record, it may be seen that the chain of circumstances narrated by the petitioner and as depicted from the records as stated supra, show that the accident was by the offending vehicle alone.
The involvement of the vehicle which was ridden by the complainant Papaiah was not at all mentioned in any of the records.
Even the police investigation papers also do not show the same.
Obviously the respondent No.1 has not contested the petition.

It is relevant to note that except the delay in filing the complaint and the divergent mentionings in the records of the NIMHANS Hospital, there - 18 - Rajaiah vs The Manager on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191853068/
7 NC: 2023:KHC:40572 is nothing on record to show that the two wheeler ridden by complainant Papaiah was involved in the accident.

sentences.text: There is nothing on record to show that Rajamma as well as her daughter were the pillion riders of the motorcycle.
The mention of the second pillion rider on the motorcycle ridden by Papaiah is nothing but a futile imagination of the respondent No.2.
It is not known on what basis, the respondent No.2 contended that there were two pillion riders on the motorcycle.
The complaint as well as the police papers and also the Hospital records which is relied by the respondent No.2 show, at the most Rajamma was a pillion rider of a two wheeler.

Therefore,
the contention of the respondent No.2 that Rajamma as well as wife of Papaiah were the pillion riders is not at all proved by any evidence.
22. The evidence on record also shows that the petitioners were the common people who were oblivious to niceties of law.
In Indian diaspora, niceties of law are not known to the common people.

In an action for tort,
- 19 - NC: 2023:KHC:40572 expecting the standards of the criminal law that a complaint should be lodged immediately after the accident cannot be expected and such expectation would only be hypertechnical.
The victims of the accident are before the Tribunal not by choice but due to the forced circumstances of the accident.
Therefore, the Tribunal should have seen that the contention of the respondent No.2 does not get any support from the medical records.

If the first information which was recorded by NIMHANS Hospital in the form of the emergency trauma care record mentioned that it was the alleged history of RTA pedestrian when crossing the road, hit by a two wheeler and subsequent entry of the same hospital also mentioned that the deceased Rajamma was pillion rider, the one which is supported by the evidence of the PW2 should have been accepted by the Tribunal, applying the preponderance of probability.
It is pertinent to note that there is absolutely no suggestion to PW2 that deceased Rajamma was in fact the pillion rider of the motorcycle ridden by Papaiah.
So also the cross examination of PW1 also do not show that there was any - 20 - NC: 2023:KHC:40572 suggestion to the above affect to him.
Under these circumstances, this Court comes to the conclusion that there was no such accident involving the motorcycle of the respondent No.1 cannot be accepted.
Clearly the Tribunal held that the motorcycle of the respondent No.2 was not involved in the accident out of the imaginary contentions raised by the respondent No.2.
It was nobody's case, except oral testimony of RW1 that Rajamma was a pillion rider.
Hence, the said finding of the Tribunal is perverse and arbitrary.
23. The petitioners are the husband, daughter and son of deceased Rajamma.
As per the post mortem report, the age of deceased Rajamma was 58 years.
Therefore, the appropriate multiplier would be 9.

Taking the notional income of the deceased Rajamma for the year 2013 at Rs.8,000/-
and by adding Rs.800/- towards future prospects, the multiplicand is held to be Rs.8,800/-.
The petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are the dependents of the deceased Rajamma.

8 show that they - 21 - NC: 2023:KHC:40572 were the dependents.

Adding Rs.48,400/- towards the loss of consortium, love and affection, and Rs.18,150/-

ORDER
The appeal is allowed.
Petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.5,78,900/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its deposit before the Tribunal.
The respondent No.2-insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of six weeks from today before the Tribunal.
The petitioner No.1 is entitled for 60% of the compensation and the petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are entitled for 20% each.
The Tribunal is at liberty to order for deposit considering the circumstances that may be brought to its notice.
